chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ali ibn al-Sindi, from Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Saeed, from a man, from Ibn Abu Yafour, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'Beware of the red camels, for they are the camels with the shortest lifespan.'
ai.seo_question: What is the reason for avoiding red camels according to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) advises avoiding red camels due to their shorter lifespan, reflecting the Shia scholarly tradition of deriving practical wisdom from observable natural phenomena. This teaching underscores the importance of selecting robust livestock for economic stability and efficient resource management in agrarian societies. It serves as a reminder that even specific biological traits can carry broader ethical implications for stewardship and care of animals.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, form Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Ali Bin Al Sandy, from Muhammad Bin Amro Bin Saeed, from a man, from Ibn Abu Yafour, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I heard him<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Beware of the red camel for it is the camel of the shortest life-span’.
en.sarwar: 10. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn Ali al-Sindiy from Muhammad ibn ‘Amr ibn Sa‘id from a man from ibn abu Ya‘fur who has said the following: “I once heard abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘
Beware of red camels because the life of such camels is the shortest.’”
